# v2 results (headline; auto-generated by `python -m beliefview.cli v2-final` / `v2-report`)

Synthetic 2D simulation. N = 200 fresh final episodes per scenario (split id 4, run once), paired across policies. Deadline T = 80 steps. Travel penalty lam = 0.004, selected on validation split id 3 by a rule fixed before any v2 episode existed. Config hash `a69bfac2342ac108`, protocol hash `005759e5dd0fd210`, core source checksum `964103366f5b5762`. Intervals are 95% percentile bootstrap over episodes (B=2000) and are **not adjusted** for the number of comparisons.

The earlier v1 record (lam = 0, config hash `222bce7e37097894`, 100 test episodes per scenario that were run twice) is kept unmodified in `results/` (top level) and `archive/v1/`. v1 and v2 use different episodes and their tables are not merged.

**What is paired.** Every policy runs the same pre-rolled episodes: identical subject trajectory, behaviour, observer start, noisy last-seen measurement and its age, deadline, sensor, look gate and controller. The detection uniform `u[t]` and the measurement noise are pre-drawn per time step and shared (common random numbers). A detection at step t happens when that step is a new look and `u[t] < P(detect | this policy's viewpoint)`, so policies at different viewpoints do **not** receive identical observations; only the draws are shared. The simulated sensor has no false positives.

## Primary comparison: clean no-miss-update ablation

BeliefView and the ablation use the same planner settings object (candidate set, horizon 12, commit 3, travel penalty lam = 0.004), the same controller and the same episodes. The only difference is whether a missed detection updates the belief. Differences are BeliefView minus ablation: `d_found` > 0 means miss updates helped; `d_rmst` < 0 means faster; distance is over all episodes (flown until first detection or the deadline).

| B_motion_mismatch | 0.68 | 0.66 | +0.015 [-0.015, +0.045] | -1.2 [-3.1, +0.6] | -3.8 [-6.0, -1.5] | 129 | 6 | 3 | 62 |

## How lam was chosen (validation split only)

Rule: select the largest lam whose combined (A+B) reacquired-by-deadline fraction is within 0.03 absolute of the best fraction on the grid; lam = 0 is not a candidate. 100 validation episodes in each of scenarios A and B (split id 3), BeliefView only, the same episodes for every candidate. Best fraction 0.620; selected lam = 0.004.

| lam | reacquired, A+B | A | B | mean travel | RMST | within 0.03 of best | selected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0005 | 0.620 (124 of 200) | 0.62 | 0.62 | 48.5 | 40.5 | yes |  |
| 0.001 | 0.620 (124 of 200) | 0.62 | 0.62 | 46.6 | 40.6 | yes |  |
| 0.002 | 0.620 (124 of 200) | 0.62 | 0.62 | 41.5 | 40.5 | yes |  |
| 0.004 | 0.605 (121 of 200) | 0.60 | 0.61 | 34.3 | 41.6 | yes | **yes** |

## Effect of the positive travel penalty: BeliefView minus the lam = 0 reference arm

The reference arm is BeliefView with lam = 0 and every other setting identical, run on the same final episodes. It is a labelled paired reference only: it was not a tuning candidate and is not a headline result. Differences are BeliefView (lam = 0.004) minus the reference arm: `d_found` < 0 means the penalty cost reacquisitions; `d_distance` < 0 means it saved travel (all episodes, flown until first detection or the deadline).
